lastMessage:
I tried to verify this live (spin up a local server + drive a headless browser), but every side-effecting command in this session right now — starting a background server, running the browser CLI, even editing `.claude/settings.json` for the permission fix — is being blocked pending approval that isn't coming through. So I can't confirm it visually right now; I went through the code by hand instead.

The CSS is correctly applied — I checked for duplicate/conflicting `#chatlog` rules and there's only the one I added (`max-height: 140px; overflow-y: auto;` plus the scrollbar styling), no conflicting override, and nothing else in the file sets `overflow: hidden` on it or an ancestor. On its face this should scroll in any standard browser.

Two likely explanations for what you're seeing:
1. **Cache** — if you're testing in an already-open browser tab, a normal refresh sometimes won't re-pull local file changes; try a hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R). If you're testing via **OBS's Browser Source**, OBS uses its own CEF cache — right-click the source → "Refresh cache of current page" (or remove/re-add it) rather than just re-clicking the scene.
2. A real edge case I found: while the "typewriter" effect is still animating a new message in, it rewrites `#chatlog`'s content every 12ms — this shouldn't reset scroll position, but if you're trying to scroll during that brief animation window it could feel unresponsive.

Can you tell me exactly how you're viewing it (which browser / OBS) and whether a hard refresh changes anything? That'll tell me whether it's a cache issue or something I'm missing in the code.

Separately: the settings.json permission fix is stuck for the same reason — the edit itself needs your approval, which should have prompted in your Claude Code UI. Can you check for that prompt and approve it?
